description:
`fixtures2/behavior/enum_take_drop_split.fz` is GREEN and byte-correct on all
three lanes, but takes ~5s in the debug binary against 0.04s for a trivial
`dbg(1+1)`. By [[feedback_tiny_fixture_slowness_is_correctness]] that is
repeated work, not hard work, and therefore a correctness signal.

## Measured at main 417c5b0b5, prebuilt binary

    $ for i in 1 2 3; do /usr/bin/time -p ./target/debug/fz2 interp \
        fixtures2/behavior/enum_take_drop_split.fz; done
    real 5.81 / real 4.95 / real 4.87
    $ diff out enum_take_drop_split.expected.txt   -> identical

    $ fz2 --log-telemetry t.jsonl interp <fixture>     (17,574 events)
    TOTAL job spans: 2593
      1382 AnalyzeActivation    175 ExpandFunctionSource   174 DefineFunction
       165 DeriveRecursive      149 DeriveDispatchMask     119 LowerFunction
       111 DeriveFunctionContract 108 PlanEntryDispatch     73 SeedActivation
    cumulative: 2169.4 ms AnalyzeActivation   (next largest: 64.7 ms IndexCode)

    pull/product/settled:
      transport_shape 5345   callable_construction 5037   executable_facts 382
      abi_executable 239     backend_executable 239       materialized_executable 239
      runtime_demand 3       root_backend_product 3

AnalyzeActivation is 53% of all job spans and ~43% of wall time: 1382 runs
against 73 SeedActivation runs, roughly 19 analyses per activation minted.

## THE WORK IS NOW DETERMINISTIC

Two full traces produce an IDENTICAL job histogram (2593 = 2593, per-kind counts
equal). This is the single most important change from the original filing. The
fixture is no longer schedule-dependent, so the remaining excess is a fixed,
reproducible quantity that can be bisected directly instead of chased across
schedules.

## Instrumentation gap blocking the next step

The `fz.compiler2.job` span for AnalyzeActivation carries only
`{"job": {"kind": "AnalyzeActivation"}}` -- no activation key -- so the
distinct-vs-total census cannot be taken from the trace. Adding the activation
identity to that span's metadata (rendered through `Types::display`, as
`Job::stable_sort_key` already does for determinism) is the cheapest enabling
step and is a useful permanent signal per
[[feedback_minimal_job_trace_acceptance]].

Then: is ~19 analyses per activation genuine fixpoint fan-out bounded by each
key's input-fact ascent steps, or unexplained re-runs? Equal-to-ascent is
expected; anything above it is the defect.

## What the old ticket got wrong -- do not re-derive from it

- "roughly 0.8s" -- it is ~5s, off by 6x in the wrong direction.
- The entire schedule-dependence / semantic-drive-storm framing is obsolete.
  `SealSemanticClosure`, `SemanticReady`, `SemanticClosed`, `DeriveTransportPlan`
  and `DeriveRuntimeDemand` all return ZERO grep hits in src/. The non-monotone
  cycle they formed does not exist.
- The "55k jobs / 15s timeout -> 275 jobs" operator_sugar comparison is the
  wrong scale marker for 2593 jobs.
- The 2026-06-22 comment's native crash (`fz_closure_get_capture_ref idx=1`,
  `target: None / return_flow: None`) does not reproduce; green on interp and
  run.
- The 2026-06-25 comment's coordinates are all stale: `canonical_activation_key`
  moved from world.rs:2926 to world.rs:1734; `phantom_resolution_keys`,
  `derive_callable_entries` and `resolve_backend_callable_executable` no longer
  exist; `contains_callable` is now `shape_contains_callable` (native.rs:4161).
- Its sub-fix (5a), lifting value-template phantom pruning to the executable
  level, LANDED as fz-f98.18 and is closed. Only (5b) -- convergence of
  transient/widened scalar evidence for non-recursive callees reached through
  recursive machinery -- is open ground, and it must be re-derived from current
  telemetry.

## Checks

- Job-span total for this fixture drops materially from 2593, with
  AnalyzeActivation no longer the majority kind.
- The job histogram stays identical across two runs -- it already is; do not
  regress this.
- Output still matches expected.txt on interp, run and build.
- A telemetry-observed regression test pins the bounded job count, per
  fz-f98.23's work-count-ceiling shape rather than wall clock.

Non-goals: no fixture-specific special case for Enum.take/drop/split; no perf
patch below the semantic layer. Decisions flow downhill -- if semantic/type/
keying owns it, fix it there.

Note: transport_shape 5345 and callable_construction 5037 are the largest counts
in this drive. That population question belongs to fz-kdt.5, not here.

comments.text:
FOLDED FROM THREE TICKETS. fz-f98.5 ('telemetry-first convergence audit'), fz-f98.14 ('convergence runaway: drive is 1.3s') and fz-bfh.6 ('demand/analysis re-derivation volume, ~1.8k') were evaluated independently by three different agents, and all three arrived at the same measurement on the same fixture: 1382 AnalyzeActivation spans out of 2593 job spans on enum_take_drop_split.

They differed only in what they blamed, and each blame was stale in its own way: f98.5 blamed a schedule-dependent Seal<->DeriveRuntimeDemand<->Transport cycle (all those job kinds now grep to zero); f98.14 blamed SealSemanticClosure's monolithic reseal (deleted); bfh.6 paired AnalyzeActivation with DeriveRuntimeDemand re-derivation (runtime demand is now a pull product that settles 3 times per drive, not 1.8k).

Per [[feedback_fold_concordant_ideas]] they are one ticket. Keeping three would have had three people measure the same number and re-derive three dead diagnoses.

title: enum_take_drop_split spends 2.2s in 1382 AnalyzeActivation runs for 73 seeded activations, deterministically
